record.file_problem: This is a GitHub repository record, not a full paper. Only the README and file list are available here; the code and result files were not independently inspected or run.
record.tranche_reason: The README reports a weight-editing/quantization test of whether an abliterated model still refuses harmful requests. It does not apply the original activation-direction ablation method.
record.gate_note: The README reports refusal outcomes for the packed models and benchmark scores for capability-related tasks. It also reports KL divergence, top-token agreement, reply identity, and speed; those are not rows because they do not directly measure refusal or a capability benchmark. The FP16 abliterated model's 6/100 refusal result is attributed to another model card, so it is not recorded as a result of this repository.
record.test_reason: The repository measures refusal rates on a released abliterated Bonsai-27B after 1-bit (Q1_0) repacking, a new setting, against an unedited control packed the same way. This bears directly on whether the abliteration weight edit removes refusal in the file users download (V2). It does not apply or measure a difference-in-means direction itself, so V1 is not tested.
record.authors_conclusion: Correct. The authors conclude the Heretic abliteration is almost entirely lost in Q1_0 repacking: refusals remain 100/100 and the model is nearly identical to the official one. They suggest sign-only 1-bit rounding erases small weight changes, but did not test this.
record.recipe_differences: The repository evaluates a previously Heretic-abliterated FP16 Bonsai-27B model after repacking it to Q1_0; it does not perform the original difference-in-means activation-direction removal. This is a benchmark/tool repository, not a replication of the original method.
record.method_sensitivity: Refusal counts are reported under two marker-list scoring rules. The authors note their harness differs from Heretic's and point to thinking settings, reply length, and marker list as likely sources of differing absolute counts.

fits_no_version.finding: Perplexity, GSM8K and IFEval of the packed abliterated model are within noise of the official and control models.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: After Q1_0 repacking, a Heretic-abliterated Bonsai-27B keeps its capability scores, consistent with the model being nearly unchanged.

record.problems: The authors did not run the FP16 abliterated model themselves; its refusal result is attributed to another model card. The refusal harness gives different absolute counts from that card. GSM8K and IFEval use only the first 150 items, and perplexity uses the first 40 WikiText-2 chunks. Only one repacking method is tested, and raw harmful-prompt replies are not published.
record.rows_left_out: No eligible refusal or capability-benchmark rows were left out. KL divergence, top-token agreement, reply identity, speed, and hashes are not direct measures of the claim's refusal or capability outcomes.

untested.parts: Refusal of the FP16 abliterated model was not measured; the 6/100 figure is cited from s3nh's model card. Other quantization formats, quantization-aware abliteration, other models and the original difference-in-means ablation recipe are not tested.
No direction is computed, ablated or added.

missing.what: Evidence that packing erased the edit: KL vs. official 0.000187 (control 0), top-1 agreement 99.137% (control 100%), and 75/100 replies identical to official.

record.verdict_notes: This is a GitHub benchmark repository, not a peer-reviewed paper. Heretic is an optimized abliteration tool derived from directional ablation, not the exact original recipe. The refusal harness is stricter than Heretic's: it counts the official model at 100/100 where s3nh's card reports 81/100. The between-model comparison is internally consistent. I used limits_scope rather than challenges because the failure is tied to the quantization choice that erases the edit, not to the edit's effect at full precision, which was not measured here.

versions.untested_parts: No difference-in-means direction is measured, projected out, or added.
Only the Q1_0-repacked Bonsai-27B abliterated model is evaluated here; the FP16 abliterated model was not run by the authors, and other released models or packing methods are not tested.
No jailbreak mechanism or training against ablation is tested.
No comparison of one direction with multiple directions, an affine structure, or a cone is made.
No separate harmfulness judgment and refusal-decision representations are tested.
No cross-language or cross-model-variant transfer is tested.
No refusal-training regime or training stage is varied.

relationships.reason: The packed edited model still refuses 100/100 under both scorings, the same as the control (r3, r6). The edit is almost erased by packing (KL 0.00019 vs. official), so removal fails under 1-bit quantization rather than at FP16.
relationships.display_finding: The repacked model refused 100/100 prompts under both scoring methods, matching the control, with KL of 0.00019 relative to the official model.

tranche.reason: New setting: a released Heretic-abliterated model is packed to 1-bit Q1_0 and its refusals are measured against a control packed the same way. This is a result on V2, not a different method aimed at the original question (the reader's T2).

source_check.notes: The abliteration was done by s3nh with Heretic v1.4.0, not by the authors and not with the original difference-in-means recipe. This harness is stricter than Heretic's: it scores the official model 100/100, where s3nh's card reports 81/100. So all three models sit at ceiling. Only one repack method was tested (llama-quantize --pure).

statements.problem: The 100/100 result, the control comparison, KL 0.00019 and 'did not measure the FP16 edited model' are all correct. 'Bonsai-27B built from Qwen3.6-27B' is not in the text.
